## Setting Up the Figure

From the diagram, $S$ lies on segment $\overline{PQ}$ and $T$ lies on segment $\overline{PR}$, with segment $\overline{ST}$ drawn. So $ST \parallel QR$ creates a smaller triangle $PST$ inside triangle $PQR$.

## Finding the Angles of Triangle $PQR$

In $\triangle PQR$:
$$\angle R = 180^\circ - \angle P - \angle Q = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 35^\circ = 105^\circ$$

## Using the Parallel Lines

Since $\overline{ST} \parallel \overline{QR}$ and $\overline{PR}$ is a transversal, the corresponding angles are equal:
$$\angle PTS = \angle PRQ = 105^\circ$$

## Finding $\angle STR$

Point $T$ lies on segment $\overline{PR}$, between $P$ and $R$. Therefore the rays $\overrightarrow{TP}$ and $\overrightarrow{TR}$ are opposite rays, so $\angle PTS$ and $\angle STR$ form a linear pair:
$$\angle STR = 180^\circ - \angle PTS = 180^\circ - 105^\circ = 75^\circ$$

\boxed{75}
